title: Ops Lab — CP commissioning & scale playbook (field notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working field-playbook for commissioning a private control plane (VPC or on-prem lab) with notes from recent Ops-lab runs. The intent is to capture pragmatic steps, Terraform module tips, scaling heuristics, and an upgrade/rotation strategy that teams can adapt. Not final — iterative, with action items at the bottom.

High-level flow (first pass):
1) Prep networking + secrets
   - Confirm VPC CIDR + peering plan with infra owner (tag: infra-vpc).
   - Create KMS keys + HSM placeholders if required by customer. Store key ARNs in tfvars secret_store.
   - Guardrail: no public EIPs on control-plane nodes during initial commissioning.

2) Terraform seed: modules + state
   - Use modules: module.network_vpc, module.bootstrap_nodes, module.controlplane_k8s, module/cp-telemetry.
   - State backend: s3 with server-side encryption + lock table (Dynamo/consul). For on-prem lab, use remote backend: rclone to object-store or HashiConsul.
   - Tip: pin module versions by git tag in root terraform registry block. Avoid floating "latest" for initial rollouts.
   - Common variables to validate: cluster_short_name, availability_zones (or rack IDs for baremetal), cp_instance_class, node_image_id, kubelet_version.

3) Bootstrap sequence (commands):
   - export TF_VAR_env=lab
   - terraform init -backend-config=backend.lab.hcl\   - terraform plan -var-file=lab.tfvars -out=plan.tfplan\   - terraform apply plan.tfplan
   - Post-apply: wait for node-provisioning job logs (kubectl -n redwood get jobs).

4) Service-level validations
   - API handshake: curl --cacert /etc/redwood/ca.pem https://controlplane.internal/healthz -> expect 200 and json {"mode":"private","replicas":n}.
   - KV cache warmup: execute synthetic workload generator (scripts/e2e/warmup.sh) for 30m to validate autoscaler hysteresis.

Terraform module notes (lessons learned):
- module.bootstrap_nodes: add a small "waiter" resource that polls the kubelet on each new host before continuing. Avoid brittle local-exec sleeps.
- module.controlplane_k8s: keep kubeadm config idempotent. Add upgrade annotation on deployments: redwood.io/last-rolled: yyyy-mm-dd to detect drift.
- module/cp-telemetry: expose a lightweight prometheus scrape target on port 9191 for early visibility.
- Exported outputs: controlplane_api_endpoint, admin_kubeconfig, bootstrap_token_expiry. Make sure outputs are redacted in CI logs.

Scaling guidance (practical):
- Start with 3 control-plane pods for HA. For small customer labs (<=4 app nodes), 3 is fine. For >8 app nodes or heavy throughput (>8k reqs/s), target 5 replicas.
- Autoscaler profile: conservative CPU headroom 30%, target latency SLO 95th percentile < 180ms for control plane API. Tune batch size and queue depth rather than just replicas.
- Edge case: when scale-up causes tail-latency spikes, enable short-term rate-limiter on ingress for new nodes and drain traffic slowly.

Rotation & Upgrade plan (zero-downtime intent):
- Strategy: rolling-recreate with canary stage. Steps:
  a) Push new control plane image to private registry with tag vX.Y.Z-canary.
  b) Deploy single canary replica in non-customer namespace, run e2e smoke and regression tests (eval prompts, token-cost sanity).
  c) If pass, roll canary into one AZ/rack at a time: cordon + drain old pod -> create new pod -> validate.
  d) Use fallback: automatic rollback to previous revision if 15% request error rate sustained for 5 minutes.
- Terraform upgrade path: treat module interface as backwards-compatible. To change sensitive inputs (e.g., instance class, network ranges), create a migration PR that runs a dry-run and documents the exact resource replacement plan.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Node bootstrap fails with image pull error -> check registry creds and repository path in tfvars; ensure NAT/Gateway for image download if no direct internet.
- Kubelet not joining -> inspect journalctl -u kubelet; common cause is time skew (chrony) or missing CRI socket.
- DB migrations blocked -> run migrations in maintenance window with read-only traffic, use small batch window and verify indices.

Runbook checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm tfstate lock and backup
- [ ] KMS keys created and IAM principals assigned
- [ ] Terraform module versions pinned
- [ ] Bootstrap nodes provisioned and kubelet ready
- [ ] Control plane health endpoints all green
- [ ] Telemetry ingest showing normal rates
- [ ] Run warmup workload for 30m
- [ ] Record baseline metrics (p95 latency, token/sec, gpu-saturation)

Notes to self / outstanding TODOs:
- Add explicit migration docs for changing cp_instance_class (defer to infra-sre review).
- Create a small utility to parse tfstate and list resources that will be replaced on apply (helpful for PR reviewers).
- Investigate intermittent DNS flips seen during last lab run (possible MTU mismatch on peered link). Add test case to lab CI.

Action items:
- Priya: draft migration checklist for network-range changes by 2025-03-10.
- Diego: add "waiter" to bootstrap module and open PR with tests (JIRA-OPS-412)
- Liam: schedule next lab run and capture perf profiles (GPU + NVMe)

References & links (working):
- Internal Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CP-bootstrapping
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/private-cp-bootstrap/pull/114
- Jira ticket: JIRA-OPS-412

If anything in here conflicts with customer-specific requirements, treat this as the ops lab starting template and adapt network/kms/registry sections accordingly.

End of notes.
